per_evidence_assessments.evidence_quote:
We conducted a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial involving 27,564 patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and LDL cholesterol levels of 70 mg per deciliter (1.8 mmol per liter) or higher who were receiving statin therapy. Patients were randomly assigned to receive evolocumab or matching placebo as subcutaneous injections. The primary efficacy end point was the composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, hospitalization for unstable angina, or coronary revascularization.

Results: Relative to placebo, evolocumab treatment significantly reduced the risk of the primary end point
per_evidence_assessments.reason: Directly describes established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease patients on statins, randomized PCSK9 inhibitor versus placebo, and reduced composite cardiovascular events.

per_evidence_assessments.evidence_quote: Relative to placebo, evolocumab treatment significantly reduced the risk of the primary end point (1344 patients [9.8%] vs. 1563 patients [11.3%]; hazard ratio, 0.85; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.79 to 0.92; P<0.001)
per_evidence_assessments.reason: Supports PCSK9 inhibitor benefit versus placebo and mentions background statin therapy in the conclusion, but this excerpted evidence gives less population detail than the full trial context.

per_evidence_assessments.evidence_quote: We conducted a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial involving 18,924 patients who had an acute coronary syndrome 1 to 12 months earlier, had an LDL cholesterol level of at least 70 mg per deciliter, and were receiving statin therapy at a high-intensity dose or at the maximum tolerated dose. Patients were randomly assigned to receive alirocumab or placebo.
per_evidence_assessments.reason: Directly matches recent acute coronary syndrome patients on statin therapy randomized to a PCSK9 inhibitor or placebo, with results and conclusion showing fewer recurrent ischemic cardiovascular events.

per_evidence_assessments.evidence_quote:
Methods: We conducted a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial involving 18,924 patients who had an acute coronary syndrome 1 to 12 months earlier, had an LDL cholesterol level of at least 70 mg per deciliter, and were receiving statin therapy at a high-intensity dose or at the maximum tolerated dose. Patients were randomly assigned to receive alirocumab or placebo. The primary end point was a composite of death from coronary heart disease, nonfatal myocardial infarction, fatal or nonfatal ischemic stroke, or unstable angina requiring hospitalization.

Results: A composite primary end-point event occurred in 903 patients (9.5%) in the alirocumab group and in 1052 patients (11.1%) in the placebo group
